title: Model serving for real-time bid scoring
prompt: A real-time bidding system must return a bid response within ~100ms at massive QPS, scoring each impression for click/conversion likelihood. How should you serve the scoring model on the bid hot path?
constraint: Hard sub-100ms bid latency at very high QPS — the auction drops late responses, and per-request compute is multiplied across millions of QPS.

options.why: Embeddings for users and ads are computed offline/near-line and cached, so the hot path only runs a small dot-product or shallow network — single-digit ms at high QPS. This fits the sub-100ms-at-massive-QPS constraint while still scoring per-request on fresh auction context. Best balance of freshness and latency.

A large per-request model gives the best accuracy but its inference latency and compute cost blow past the budget once multiplied across millions of QPS — tail latencies exceed 100ms and you drop bids. The constraint explicitly rules out heavy per-request compute on the hot path.

A pure cache lookup is the fastest possible path and trivially meets latency, so it's defensible. But precomputing every (user x ad x context) combination is infeasible and the scores ignore real-time auction signals, hurting accuracy. Latency-safe but too coarse — weaker than scoring online over cached embeddings.

Offloading to a separate inference service adds a network round trip plus queueing on every bid; under massive QPS that tail latency alone often exceeds the entire 100ms budget. Directly violates the latency constraint regardless of model quality.
